headlines.text: That Saturday in 2020, there was a changing of the guard for the AEW Women's World Title as Hikaru Shida vs. Nyla Rose battled it out, appearing on Double or Nothing, rated 8.13 ? an excellent showing ? ending the champion's reign at 1 defense. An emotional title win, widely believed to be dedicated to the memory of the late Hana Kimura ? Shida absorbed a brutal kendo stick beatdown before turning the tables and claiming the AEW Women's World Championship for the first time.

On a Saturday in 2020, back when history was made as Cody vs. Lance Archer contested the very first AEW TNT Title match, appearing on Double or Nothing, rated 6.22. The final of the inaugural TNT Title tournament, with Mike Tyson personally presenting the brand-new championship ? Cody took some wild bumps against the much larger Archer before claiming the title to become AEW's first-ever TNT Champion.

On a Saturday in 2020, back when Jon Moxley vs. Brodie Lee clashed for the AEW World Heavyweight Title, appearing on Double or Nothing, rated 8.13 ? a genuinely great match. It was the first title opportunity of Brodie Lee's career. A dangerous main event, with security guards literally separating the two before the bell rang ? Lee kicked out of two Paradigm Shifts before Moxley finally choked him unconscious with a rear naked choke to retain the title.

secondaries.text: On this day in 2020, Omega & Page vs. The Young Bucks vs. The Inner Circle (Guevara & Jericho) vs. Proud-N-Powerful vs. Adam Page vs. Kenny Omega vs. Matt Jackson vs. Nick Jackson vs. Matt Hardy vs. Chris Jericho vs. Sammy Guevara vs. Ortiz vs. Santana vs. Jake Hager fought it out in a Stadium Stampede match, in the show-closing main event slot on Double or Nothing, rated 9.22 ? a match that lived up to every bit of hype ? part of a stacked Double or Nothing '20 card, rated 8.28 overall. A groundbreaking cinematic brawl, staged at the 50-yard line of the Jacksonville Jaguars' stadium ? the culmination of the Elite/Inner Circle war, and a wildly creative match many still call one of the best cinematic matches AEW has ever produced.

On a Saturday in 2020, back when Brian Cage made their AEW debut in a Ladder match against Colt Cabana vs. Darby Allin vs. Frankie Kazarian vs. Kip Sabian vs. Joey Janela vs. Luchasaurus vs. Orange Cassidy vs. Scorpio Sky, appearing on Double or Nothing, rated 5.35.
Flash back to 2020, when it marked the first-ever meeting between Kris Statlander and Penelope Ford on Double or Nothing, rated 4.34.
